newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis wound two Palestinians in Gaza clash.
newsitem.headline: Israelis wound two Palestinians in Gaza clash.

text.p: Israeli soldiers shot and wounded two Palestinians in Gaza on Thursday in clashes with hundreds of Arabs who planted olive trees on land seized by Jewish settlers, hospital officials and witnesses said.

Witnesses said other Palestinians were overcome by tear gas and beaten by Israeli soldiers during the clash which erupted after some 600 demonstrators knocked down a fence erected by residents of Morag settlement earlier this month.
Palestinians, who said the fence effectively annexed a privately-owned plot next to the settlement, had been holding a tent vigil at the site since the settlers erected the fence on June 2.

"They fired live ammunition in the air and tear gas and rubber bullets at the crowd," a witness told Reuters. He said Israeli soldiers also beat demonstrators before Palestinian police stepped in to hold demonstrators back.
A cloud of tear gas hung over the area as Palestinian protesters battled troops in the sandy field.
Israeli military sources said soldiers and Palestinian police dispersed hundreds of demonstrators who threw rocks at the fence. They made no mention of casualties.
An elderly Palestinian died at a tent on the site apparently from a heart attack, a doctor at the Khan Younis hospital said. He said he could not say if the man had been affected by the tear gas.
Israeli soldiers guarding the Morag enclave have deployed tanks in the area.
Khan Younis hospital director said a middle aged Palestinian was shot in the chest and a bullet grazed the head of another Arab. Neither was in critical condition.
The clashes ended when Palestinian police managed to restrain the demonstrators and separate them from the Israelis.

An Israeli spokesman said earlier this month the fence was intended to protect flower plantations from thieves. He said contacts were underway with the Palestinian side to determine if the fence intruded on private property.
Palestinian-Israeli tension has been running high since the Jewish state began building a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March, prompting clashes in parts of the West Bank.

Also on Thursday, Israel dedicated a controversial memorial in Gaza erected for a soldier killed in September during clashes with PLO police following Israel's opening of a tourist tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem, witnesses said. Fifteen Israeli soldiers and 61 Palestinians were killed in the clashes.
Palestinians protested near the site, saying the memorial had been built on land under Palestinian jurisdiction.
